tEn: CMG Exclusive: Elon Musk on China's Unmatched Charm
tZh: 总台专访马斯克：中国的魅力无以言表
sEn: Tesla CEO Elon Musk sits down with CCTV Finance to discuss China's remarkable progress, Tesla's Shanghai Gigafactory, and the future of humanoid robots and AI.
sZh: 特斯拉 CEO 埃隆·马斯克接受央视财经专访，畅谈中国市场的巨大进步、特斯拉上海超级工厂以及人形机器人和 AI 的未来。

consensus.en: China excels at manufacturing, with Tesla Shanghai a gem of quality and efficiency.
consensus.zh: 中国在制造业上优势显著，特斯拉上海工厂是质量与效率的明珠。

consensus.en: AI progress is shockingly fast, with breakthroughs occurring multiple times daily.
consensus.zh: AI 进步快得惊人，每天都会出现多次突破。

consensus.en: Chinese AI models are outstanding, achieving best performance per unit of compute.
consensus.zh: 中国 AI 模型表现出色，实现了单位算力的最佳性能。

consensus.en: Full and rapid rocket reusability is the fundamental breakthrough for multi-planetary life.
consensus.zh: 火箭的完全快速可复用是实现多行星生命的基础性突破。

consensus.en: Humanoid robots will exceed 1 billion within 10 years, amplifying productivity.
consensus.zh: 人形机器人将在 10 年内超过 10 亿台，大幅提升生产力。

consensus.en: AI safety requires a US-China working committee to apply fair regulation globally.
consensus.zh: AI 安全需要美中联合工作组，在全球范围内公平实施监管。

contrarian.en: China will overcome compute constraints via lithography in about 2-3 years.
contrarian.zh: 中国将在约 2-3 年内通过光刻技术突破算力限制。

contrarian.en: In the abundant future, money may not matter as goods exceed consumption.
contrarian.zh: 在富足的未来，货币可能不再重要，因为商品将超过消费需求。

contrarian.en: Robots will saturate human demand and then work for themselves.
contrarian.zh: 机器人将满足人类所有需求，然后为自己工作。

contrarian.en: Grok will catch up to frontier models next year using SpaceX and Tesla data.
contrarian.zh: Grok 将利用 SpaceX 和特斯拉的数据，在明年赶上前沿模型。

contrarian.en: AI will excel at real-world engineering, not just software engineering.
contrarian.zh: AI 将在现实世界工程中表现出色，而不仅仅是软件工程。

contrarian.en: Neuralink aims to solve human bandwidth constraints for better AI alignment.
contrarian.zh: Neuralink 旨在解决人类带宽限制，以实现更好的 AI 对齐。

turns.en: Thank you so much, Elon, for joining me, and also having us here at Tesla Global Engineering Headquarters. It's so amazing to see new technology innovations and all the talented engineers here as well.
turns.zh: 非常感谢你，Elon，接受我的采访，也感谢你让我们来到特斯拉全球工程总部。能看到这些新技术创新，还有这里这么多有才华的工程师，真是太棒了。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: In May, you were also on the delegation to China. You met with President Xi. What's your impression about President Xi as a leader?
turns.zh: 今年 5 月，你也随代表团去了中国，还见了习主席。作为一位领导人，你对习主席的印象如何？

turns.en: Well, he seems like a great leader. I mean, under his tenure, China has prospered immensely. I've seen it firsthand. If you visit China, you see the amount of progress that happens from one year to the next, or even within a year. It's very visible. You can see the new buildings, the new infrastructure. And it's also obvious just walking around the streets — the increased prosperity of the average Chinese citizen has increased tremendously. And that's happened under President Xi's tenure, while he's been the leader of China. So he's clearly done an excellent job and is very capable.
turns.zh: 嗯，他看起来是一位伟大的领导人。我的意思是，在他任内，中国取得了巨大的繁荣。这是我亲眼所见。如果你去中国，你会看到一年到下一年、甚至一年之内发生的进步有多大。这非常明显。你能看到新的建筑、新的基础设施。而且只要在街上走走就很明显——普通中国民众的富裕程度大幅提升了。而这都发生在习主席任内，在他担任中国领导人期间。所以他显然做得非常出色，也非常有能力。

turns.en: Tesla Gigafactory Shanghai has always done an incredible job. You've praised your teams many times.
turns.zh: 特斯拉上海超级工厂一直做得非常出色。你也多次称赞过你的团队。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So what kind of advantage or breakthroughs do you think make the Shanghai factory such an important position in Tesla's global blueprint? And what ultimate confidence do you think this will unfold, especially in the market?
turns.zh: 那你认为是什么样的优势或突破，让上海工厂在特斯拉的全球蓝图中占据如此重要的位置？你觉得这最终会带来怎样的信心，尤其是在市场上？

turns.en: Well, China just has a very strong inherent ability to do manufacturing well. And this has been true not just in present days, but for the past two or three thousand years. I think that, to be totally frank, the magic of Tesla Shanghai is —
turns.zh: 嗯，中国本身就有着非常强的制造业天赋。这不仅在当下如此，在过去两三千年里都是如此。我觉得，坦白说，特斯拉上海的魔力在于——

turns.en: Because of Chinese — to be totally — because it's in China, at least, right?
turns.zh: 因为中国人——坦白说——至少是因为它在中国，对吧？

turns.en: Yes. What we have is the Tesla China team is just incredibly talented and hardworking and trustworthy. And they have excellent quality and excellent efficiency. So the Tesla Shanghai factory is a gem. It's beautiful, actually, if anyone's ever been there. And we also care a lot about taking care of the workers and making sure they have good health care and good food and enjoy coming to work. It's very important.
turns.zh: 是的。我们拥有的是特斯拉中国团队，他们非常有才华、勤奋、值得信赖。他们的质量出色，效率也出色。所以特斯拉上海工厂是一颗明珠。它很美，真的，如果有人去过那里的话。我们也很在意照顾好工人，确保他们有好的医疗、好的伙食，并且享受来上班。这非常重要。

turns.en: Absolutely. I think we can tell that all your staff at the Shanghai factory really enjoy working there.
turns.zh: 确实如此。我觉得能看出来，你上海工厂的所有员工都很享受在那里工作。

turns.en: So, talking about the next hot topic recently — we could probably call September the Cybercab month. Have you seen the videos, like all the people gathering around it? It goes very, very quickly.
turns.zh: 那说到最近的下一个热门话题——我们大概可以把 9 月称为 Cybercab 之月。你看到那些视频了吗，就是所有人围着它的那些？传播得非常非常快。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, it's pretty cool, because we designed the car to look futuristic. From a fashion standpoint, we don't want the aesthetics of the street to stay stagnant. You want to evolve what cars look like. And also, I think maybe even clothing. There was rapid fashion evolution in the '50s, '60s, '70s, '80s, '90s, and it's probably time to make things look more futuristic.
turns.zh: 是的。我的意思是，这挺酷的，因为我们把这辆车设计得很有未来感。从时尚的角度看，我们不希望街道的美学停滞不前。你要让汽车的样子不断进化。而且我觉得，也许连服装也是。50 年代、60 年代、70 年代、80 年代、90 年代都有快速的时尚演变，现在大概也是时候让东西看起来更有未来感了。

turns.en: And then how do you see the market potential for Cybercab? It's really futuristic, but how long can it really come to reality, to real life?
turns.zh: 那你怎么看 Cybercab 的市场潜力？它真的很有未来感，但它要多久才能真正成为现实、走进真实生活？

turns.en: Well, we have the Cybercab, which, as you know, has no steering wheel or pedals or side mirrors or rearview mirror, operating commercially in Texas right now. And it will soon be operating commercially in Florida and Nevada and a number of other states. And probably by the middle of next year, it'll be operating commercially in California.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们有 Cybercab，如你所知，它没有方向盘、没有踏板、没有侧后视镜、也没有后视镜，目前正在得克萨斯州商业化运营。很快它也会在佛罗里达、内华达以及其他一些州商业化运营。大概到明年年中，它会在加利福尼亚商业化运营。

turns.en: Absolutely. I think all the changes are happening really fast. It's just like every day we have to look at social media to see the kind of improvements or breakthroughs about AI or other tech topics.
turns.zh: 确实如此。我觉得所有变化都发生得非常快。就像每天我们都得刷社交媒体，看看 AI 或其他科技话题有什么改进或突破。

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, AI is just so crazy. The rate of AI software improvements and major announcements is so rapid that it makes my head spin. And I'm in AI, and it still makes my head spin.
turns.zh: 是啊，我的意思是，AI 简直太疯狂了。AI 软件改进和重大发布的速度如此之快，让我头晕目眩。我自己就在做 AI，它还是让我头晕目眩。

turns.en: You're in the industry, but you still have to —
turns.zh: 你就在这个行业里，但你还是得——

turns.en: It's still shocking. Sometimes when I go to bed there'll be some big AI breakthrough, and then when I wake up there's an AI breakthrough, and by the time it gets to lunch there's another AI breakthrough.
turns.zh: 它仍然令人震惊。有时候我睡觉时会有某个重大的 AI 突破，然后我醒来时又有一个 AI 突破，等到午饭时又有另一个 AI 突破。

turns.en: Exactly. So that's why even during this break you have to check some others.
turns.zh: 没错。所以就算在这次休息期间，你也得看看别的。

turns.en: Yeah, I probably have to check some others.
turns.zh: 是啊，我大概得看看别的。

turns.en: So talking about AI models, Tesla had the latest version, right? The latest release about Grok 4.7.
turns.zh: 那说到 AI 模型，特斯拉有最新的版本，对吧？关于 Grok 4.7 的最新发布。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: I think this is your most focused thing these two days. I just saw you post on social saying that the Grok bot is already in your Tesla. Tell us what the reactions are, what's the latest you have received.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是你这两天最关注的事。我刚看到你在社交媒体上发帖说，Grok 机器人已经装进你的特斯拉了。跟我们说说反响如何，你收到的最新反馈是什么？

turns.en: Yeah. Well, we release a new model roughly every month or two. And Grok 4.7 is a cool model. It's a solid workhorse of a model. It's not as good as, say, Opus 5.5 that just got released. But also, we've only been around for about three years doing AI, whereas Anthropic's been around for six years. So I would expect that we probably catch up to the frontier sometime next year, most likely. In the meantime, I think Grok is very useful for many things. And Grok bot, which is kind of like a personal digital assistant, has been very popular and is growing about 100% a month. So it's growing very rapidly.
turns.zh: 是的。嗯，我们大概每一两个月发布一个新模型。Grok 4.7 是个很酷的模型。它是一个扎实的主力模型。它不如刚发布的 Opus 5.5 那么好。但话说回来，我们做 AI 才大约三年，而 Anthropic 已经做了六年。所以我预计我们大概会在明年某个时候追上前沿，很可能是这样。与此同时，我觉得 Grok 在很多事情上都很有用。而 Grok 机器人，它有点像个人数字助理，一直非常受欢迎，每月增长约 100%。所以它增长得非常快。

turns.en: I think you're very humble saying that Grok 4.7 is not a perfect wine, but we know that although it has experienced a little bit of delay, people are already very fascinated or interested to know, because Grok 4.7 is already being trained by SpaceX real-world engineering data. So, do you think —
turns.zh: 我觉得你很谦虚，说 Grok 4.7 不是一瓶完美的酒，但我们知道，尽管它经历了一点延迟，人们已经非常着迷、非常想知道，因为 Grok 4.7 已经在用 SpaceX 的真实世界工程数据训练了。所以，你觉得——

turns.en: Only a little bit so far.
turns.zh: 到目前为止只用了一点点。

turns.en: A little bit. Okay. So do you think this will be one of your secret weapons to break through the AGI ceiling, because currently the models have the challenge for data?
turns.zh: 一点点。好的。那你觉得这会是你突破 AGI 天花板（通用人工智能）的秘密武器之一吗？因为目前这些模型都面临数据的挑战。

turns.en: Yes. Well, I think we've got a real opportunity with the SpaceX training data and maybe with the Tesla training data to make AI extremely capable in real-world engineering. So what Anthropic did extremely well was make AI excellent at software engineering. But no one has yet made AI excellent at real-world engineering.
turns.zh: 是的。嗯，我觉得我们有一个真正的机会，用 SpaceX 的训练数据、也许还有特斯拉的训练数据，让 AI 在真实世界工程方面变得极其强大。Anthropic 做得极其出色的一点，是让 AI 在软件工程方面非常优秀。但还没有人让 AI 在真实世界工程方面变得优秀。

transcript.sec: Chinese AI Models and Compute Constraints

turns.en: You mentioned many times previously that Chinese models are also doing a fascinating job. So currently, what are the most impressive breakthroughs for Chinese models in your understanding?
turns.zh: 你之前多次提到，中国的模型也做得非常出色。那么目前，在你看来，中国模型最令人印象深刻的突破是什么？

turns.en: Well, Chinese AI models are generally outstanding, actually. I mean, you can see on the intelligence rankings, especially given the limited amount of compute that the Chinese AI companies have, the performance is excellent. I'd rate probably China as being by far the best in terms of performance per unit of compute. And as I've said publicly, I think China's going to address the compute limitation faster than most people expect. My rough guess would be that China addresses the compute constraints with lithography and chip making in about two or three years.
turns.zh: 嗯，中国的 AI 模型总体上确实非常出色。你看智能排行榜就能发现，尤其是考虑到中国 AI 公司拥有的算力有限，其表现依然非常优秀。我大概会认为，中国在单位算力性能方面遥遥领先。而且正如我公开说过的，我认为中国解决算力限制的速度会比大多数人预期的更快。我粗略估计，中国大约会在两到三年内通过光刻和芯片制造解决算力约束。

turns.en: Two or three years. We will really be expecting to this time. So what are the challenges facing AGI? In early September, in the G20 visual session, you raised a very serious concern about the compute and electricity shortages. You mentioned that probably China has way more capability about electricity infrastructure. Yes. And can you elaborate a little bit more about this gap? And you know, what areas do you think the Chinese industry and capability can help to get a new breakthrough for specifically on the electricity infrastructure for the whole world?
turns.zh: 两到三年。我们真的会期待这个时间点。那么 AGI 面临哪些挑战？在九月初的 G20 视频会议上，你对算力和电力短缺提出了非常严重的担忧。你提到中国可能在电力基础设施方面能力更强。是的。你能再详细谈谈这个差距吗？以及你认为中国产业和能力在哪些领域可以帮助全世界在电力基础设施方面取得新的突破？

turns.en: It was just a statement of fact that China, like earlier this year, China passed the electricity output of the United States, Europe, and India combined. Wow. Yeah. And continuing to increase significantly. So if China reaches the same GDP electricity output of the US, which I think is likely, then China would go from where it is now roughly three times the US electricity production to probably four times, which would be proportionate to the population difference.
turns.zh: 这只是陈述一个事实：今年早些时候，中国的电力产出超过了美国、欧洲和印度的总和。哇。是的。而且还在持续大幅增长。所以如果中国达到与美国相同的 GDP 电力产出，我认为这很有可能，那么中国将从现在大约是美国电力生产的三倍，增长到可能是四倍，这与人口差异成比例。

turns.en: Talking about the topic like AI safety, what kind of crucial consensus do you expect?
turns.zh: 谈到 AI 安全这个话题，你期望达成什么样的关键共识？

turns.en: Yeah, I think maybe there could be a working committee to figure out safety. Because in order for safety to work, it can't just be regulation in the US or regulation in China. It's got to be, you know, how do we apply regulation fairly to AI produced in any country, but really China and the US are the ones that really matter here. So I think a really important thing that would be good for the safety of AI for all of humanity.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为也许可以成立一个工作委员会来研究安全问题。因为要让安全措施奏效，不能只是美国或中国的监管。必须是，你知道，我们如何公平地对任何国家生产的 AI 应用监管，但真正重要的是中国和美国。所以我认为这对全人类的 AI 安全来说是一件非常重要的事情。

turns.en: Yeah. So let's talk about the humanoid robotics because I think this is also a kind of industrial field US-China can still work together leading the world. And also I can give you one example for the Optimus. It's really amazing, really impressive. So before interview, we had a kind of interactions. We played rock, paper, scissors with Optimus.
turns.zh: 是的。那么我们来谈谈人形机器人，因为我认为这也是中美可以共同引领世界的一个工业领域。而且我可以给你举一个擎天柱的例子。它真的非常惊人，非常令人印象深刻。所以在采访之前，我们进行了一些互动。我们和擎天柱玩了石头剪刀布。

turns.en: Oh, yeah. Okay.
turns.zh: 哦，是的。好的。

turns.en: Yeah, we just won the first two rounds, and Optimus won all the remaining. That's really impressive.
turns.zh: 是的，我们只赢了前两轮，擎天柱赢了剩下的所有。这真的非常令人印象深刻。

turns.en: Well, robots have a very fast reaction time, so it's going to be very difficult to beat a robot for reaction time. Because we are somewhat constrained by our biology. But a robot, you can just improve the actuators, improve the sensors, improve the frame rate of the cameras, increase the amount of AI compute, and it's going to just fundamentally be much better, and have faster reactions than humans. I enjoyed watching the robot games. I mean, everyone in America was fascinated by that, but
